air.keywords: air eq high shelf top end sheen brightness presence open treble mastering vocals
slider_desc: How much air: up to +9 dB of gentle high shelf, its corner moving from 16 kHz down to 10 kHz as the amount grows; 0 is flat.
uses: Opening up a dull mix or master
Adding sheen to vocals and acoustic guitars
Lifting cymbals and room tone without harshness
A last touch of brightness on a bus
air.properties: Input → RBJ high shelf (slope 0.5, 0..+9 dB, corner 16 kHz → 10 kHz with the amount, held below 0.45 × sample rate) → Output. Zero latency, stereo channels processed independently.

tone.keywords: tone eq bass treble baxandall hi-fi shelf low high warm bright simple console channel
slider_desc: Low shelf gain, ±12 dB.
High shelf gain, ±12 dB.
Corner of the low shelf.
Corner of the high shelf.
Output level after the shelves.
uses: Quick tone shaping of a track or bus
Adding warmth or weight to thin sources
Taming dull or harsh recordings
A hi-fi style loudness curve
tone.properties: Input → two first-order shelves (one-pole low-passes at Bass Freq and Treble Freq, 6 dB per octave, never ringing) → Output gain. Flat at 0 dB. Zero latency, stereo channels processed independently.

glue_comp.keywords: glue compressor bus buss mix console stereo link auto release parallel sidechain hpf drums mastering
slider_desc: Level above which the compressor starts to work (4 dB soft knee around it).
Compression ratio: 2:1 for gentle glue, 4:1 for control, 10:1 for heavy squash.
How fast the gain reduction sets in; slower attacks let transients through.
How fast the gain recovers; Auto follows the program (fast after peaks, slow under dense passages).
Gain after compression.
Blend between the dry and the compressed signal (parallel compression).
High-pass on the detector only, so bass does not pump the mix (0 = off).
uses: Gluing a mix bus together
Punchy drum bus compression
Parallel (New York) compression
Gentle control on a master or a group
glue_comp.properties: Input → key (optional one-pole high-pass) → stereo-linked peak detector → gain computer (2/4/10:1, 4 dB soft knee) → smoothing in dB (stepped attack 0.1–30 ms, release 0.1–1.2 s or Auto: the deeper of an 80 ms and a 0.5 s / 1.5 s envelope) → Makeup → Dry/Wet Mix → Output. Zero latency.

console_channel.keywords: console channel analog mixer desk summing saturation colour warm punchy bright drive harmonics tape track
slider_desc: Clean: no emphasis, symmetric saturation. Warm: the lows saturate first, with even harmonics. Punchy: the deep lows saturate first, with more drive. Bright: the highs saturate first.
How hard the channel is driven: up to 12, 15 or 18 dB depending on the character; small signals stay clean.
Output level after the console stage.
uses: Analog-desk colour on every track of a mix
Warming up thin digital sources
Adding weight and punch to drums and bass
Use with Console Buss on the bus the tracks feed
console_channel.properties: Input → first-order pre-emphasis shelf (per character) → soft saturator (Padé tanh, 6 dB of headroom, even harmonics for Warm and Punchy) → the exact inverse shelf (flat response at low level) → 5 Hz DC blocker → Output. Zero latency, stereo channels processed independently.

console_buss.keywords: console buss bus master analog mixer desk summing saturation crosstalk colour warm punchy bright drive glue mix
slider_desc: Clean: no emphasis, symmetric saturation. Warm: the lows saturate first, with even harmonics. Punchy: the deep lows saturate first. Bright: the highs saturate first.
How hard the bus is driven (up to 9 or 12 dB depending on the character), and how much the sides leak into each other (up to -30 dB).
Output level after the console stage.
uses: Analog summing colour on the mix bus
Pairing with Console Channel on the tracks
Gentle density on drum and music busses
A touch of desk crosstalk for a less clinical stereo image
console_buss.properties: Input → first-order pre-emphasis shelf (per character) → soft saturator (Padé tanh, 8 dB of headroom) → the exact inverse shelf → crosstalk (the other side high-passed at 1 kHz, up to -30 dB with Drive) → 5 Hz DC blocker → Output. Zero latency.

space.keywords: reverb space room chamber hall galaxy algorithmic fdn ambience long decay modulation pre-delay vocals pads
slider_desc: The kind of space: Room (short, close), Chamber (dense), Hall (big and smooth) or Galaxy (huge, long and moving).
How big the space is, from half to twice its type's size.
How long the tail lasts: Room 0.2 to 1.5 s, Chamber 0.5 to 3 s, Hall 1 to 8 s, Galaxy 3 to 30 s.
How fast the highs die away compared with the rest of the tail.
How much the delay lines drift, for a smooth, chorused tail without metallic ringing.
Time before the reverb starts, to keep the dry sound clear.
Blend between the dry and the reverberated signal.
uses: Rooms and chambers on drums and vocals
Concert halls on strings, piano and choirs
Huge ambient tails on pads and sound design
Putting a whole mix in one space
space.properties: Input → Pre-Delay → two Schroeder all-passes per side → 8-line feedback delay network (moving interpolated reads, one-pole damping, 60 dB decay in the decay time, 8×8 Hadamard matrix) → left from the even lines, right from the odd → Dry/Wet Mix → Output. Zero latency.
